learning_outcomes.text: Identify different styles of interpersonal relationships and determine the most adequate behavioral, attitudinal and relational factors for the efficiency of each professional communication situation.

Apply attitudes that generate satisfaction in the professional environment and practical communication techniques to manage interaction situations whose demands and/or difficulties imply a high level of control over the communication process.

Self-diagnose needs for the evolution of their communication potential and be aware of the changes to be promoted to ensure a strong proficiency in their communication performance in the exercise of professional functions in the areas of engineering and information, communication and electronics technologies.

Exercise highly effective communication in the work context, as a key factor for self-improvement throughout the career in the areas of engineering and technologies, mainly related to Information, Communication and Electronics Technologies (TICE).

syllabus_topics: QUALITY IN CUSTOMER SERVICE (INTERNAL / EXTERNAL) Concept of quality, customer perception and loyalty to the company
Identify and satisfy customer motivational needs
Use of attitudes that facilitate and block professional relationship
MANAGEMENT OF COMMUNICATIONAL ATTITUDES IN INTERACTION Characterization of attitudes and identification of their behavioral effects
Competitive versus resolving processes and the use of empathy in communication
Practical applications and implications at the level of interpersonal relationship
COMMUNICATION IN TECHNICAL INTERVENTIONS Objectives, contexts, moments and forms of intervention
Knowing how to "shut up" and adapt to different types of customers
Practical guide for application in professional situations
SUPPORT AND TROUBLESHOOTING Assistance with the specific difficulties of each interlocutor
Solving approach to personal and/or professional problems
Practical guide to guide procedures in communication interaction
teaching_methods: Interrogative method (presentations with discussion with the participants)
assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as 40% In-person participation (PC) and 60% Assessment Test (AT). Final approval requires a minimum score of 50% in PC and 50% in AT, with a total sum of at least 9.5 out of 20. Students failing only the assessment test may access an appeal period exam, which will be weighted at 60%. Classification improvement is also possible via an appeal season exam, weighted at 60%, and exempted students are assessed 100% via the Assessment Test or Appeal Exam.
